name: Visual Presentation
explanation: This criterion applies to blocks of text — paragraphs of body copy, not headings or single lines. It requires a mechanism letting users customize how that text is presented, covering five properties. Users can choose their own foreground and background colors. Text can be constrained to no more than 80 characters per line. Text is not fully justified — a ragged right edge is required, since justified text stretches word spacing in ways that make lines harder to track for some readers. Line spacing within a paragraph is at least 1.5 times the font size, and paragraph spacing is at least 1.5 times that. Text can be resized up to 200% without needing to scroll horizontally. The site doesn't have to force all of these as the default appearance, but a user must be able to select or adjust each one, whether through a site-provided display mode or the page simply not fighting the user's own browser settings with hard-coded colors or fixed widths.
whoItAffects: People with low vision who need a specific high-contrast color combination to read comfortably are blocked when a site hard-codes its own colors and ignores user style sheets. People with dyslexia or other reading disabilities lose their place on very long lines of text, or find justified text's uneven word gaps create distracting 'rivers' of whitespace. People with cognitive or attention-related disabilities rely on generous line and paragraph spacing to visually separate ideas and avoid losing their place. Anyone using browser zoom or a mobile device needs text to reflow into a single readable column instead of forcing horizontal scrolling.
howToTest: Pick a page with a paragraph of body text. First, check line length: resize the browser window to full width and confirm text doesn't stretch into very long lines, roughly 80 characters or fewer. Second, look at the right edge of the paragraph — if every line ends flush at the same right margin, the text is justified and fails this check. Third, zoom to 200% and confirm you can still read every line without scrolling sideways. Finally, try your browser's reader mode or a high-contrast mode and confirm the page's own styles don't override your chosen colors or spacing.

check.question: A site displays article body text fully justified (flush on both left and right edges) with a line-height of 1. Which part of SC 1.4.8 (Visual Presentation) does this fail, and why?
choices: It fails because justified text with tight line spacing is harder to read for some users — both the ragged-right and 1.5x line-spacing sub-requirements are violated
It doesn't fail anything, since SC 1.4.8 only concerns color contrast
It fails only because justified text is always invalid HTML
It fails because line-height of 1 makes the text too small to resize
